summary: An autonomous early warning system correlating astronaut biometrics with cabin environmental telemetry under NASA-STD-3001 standards.
details:
Astronaut Health Monitoring Interface This project is developed as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge and focuses on the design of a digital interface for monitoring astronaut health and spacecraft cabin conditions. Its primary objective is to present relevant health and environmental information through a structured, accessible, and user-friendly platform designed for the context of human space exploration. The interface incorporates multiple monitoring categories, including skeletal and muscular system health, as well as spacecraft cabin conditions. These categories address important aspects of astronaut well-being during space missions, particularly the physiological challenges associated with microgravity and the importance of maintaining suitable living and working conditions aboard spacecraft. By consolidating these categories within a unified interface, the project aims to facilitate the visualization and organization of relevant information. An additional feature of the project is its support for ten different language options, promoting accessibility for users from diverse linguistic backgrounds. The interface is designed to present information clearly and consistently, allowing users to navigate between monitoring sections and access the available data efficiently. Through the integration of health-related monitoring categories, cabin condition indicators, and multilingual functionality, this project explores the role of interface design in supporting the presentation and interpretation of astronaut health information. It represents a conceptual approach to improving the accessibility and organization of information relevant to human spaceflight. The project is intended as an interface design concept rather than a validated medical monitoring or diagnostic system. Its practical application would require appropriate data sources, validated measurement systems, and further development to support operational use in space missions.
